description: Equipo de la UPIIAP participando en el NASA Space Apps Challenge en el reto The Earth Information Jukebox.
summary: Earth Jukebox is a web app to turn NASA Earth visualizations into sound. We took 15 frames from three different NASA datasets (night lights, global temperatures, and Antarctic ice loss) and wrote a Python script that analyzes the warmth, brightness, and visual changes in each image to generate notes on an A minor pentatonic scale. Our goal is to make climate data more accessible, especially for blind and visually impaired people, by turning visual charts into an interactive audio experience.
details:
Our project, Earth Jukebox, takes visualizations from NASA's Earth Information Center and uses a Python script to map warmth, brightness, and changes across 15 frames, turning them into 30-second audio tracks based on the A minor pentatonic scale.

It creates a multisensory experience that allows blind or visually impaired people to perceive climate and planetary changes through sound.

We want NASA's Earth science data to be more inclusive, going beyond the purely visual.

We used the Python language and Google Colab to process the frames and generate the audio.

Instead of using static charts, we transformed satellite data into an interactive Jukebox, visualizing the notes in real time.
